accepted.s: Which one of the following best describes a pressure group?
o: A constitutional body that supervises the conduct of elections
A temporary administrative committee constituted by the government
An organised group that seeks to influence public policy without contesting elections or seeking office
An organised group that contests elections to capture political power
accepted.x: A pressure group seeks to influence public policy but does not contest elections or seek governmental office.
accepted.tq: Distinguish influence on policy from contesting elections and holding office.
accepted.sec: Pressure groups - definition, types, most influential, techniques  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding stakeholders in governance:
1. The State, Market and Civil Society constitute three broad sets of stakeholders in governance.
2. Pressure groups, trade unions and NGOs belong to civil society.
3. Ministers and Members of Parliament are classified as pressure groups because they influence public policy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The State, Market and Civil Society are the three broad sets of governance stakeholders, and pressure groups, trade unions and NGOs belong to civil society. Ministers and MPs are not pressure groups merely because they influence policy.
accepted.tq: Identify the wrong classification of public actors.
accepted.sec: Pressure groups - definition, types, most influential, techniques  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT generally regarded as a pressure group?
o: A group of Members of Parliament acting in their legislative capacity
accepted.x: Trade unions, NGOs and business associations may function as pressure groups. MPs acting as legislators are not classified as pressure groups.
accepted.tq: Find the institutional actor that does not belong to the pressure-group category.
accepted.sec: Pressure groups - definition, types, most influential, techniques  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:

List-I (Type of pressure group)
A. Business
B. Trade union
C. Professional
D. Peasant

List-II (Example)
1. Indian Medical Association
2. Bharatiya Kisan Union
3. FICCI
4. AITUC

option_a: A-3, B-4, C-1, D-2
option_b: A-4, B-3, C-2, D-1
option_c: A-3, B-1, C-4, D-2
option_d: A-2, B-4, C-1, D-3
accepted.x: FICCI is a business group, AITUC is a trade union, the Indian Medical Association is a professional group, and Bharatiya Kisan Union is a peasant organisation.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes with mismatched group types.
accepted.sec: Pressure groups - definition, types, most influential, techniques  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Professional pressure group — Bar Council of India
accepted.x: Jamaat-e-Islami Hind is listed as a religious pressure group. Peasant pressure groups include Bharatiya Kisan Union and All India Kisan Sabha.
accepted.tq: Use the type-example mismatch to identify the incorrect pair.

accepted.s: Almond and Powell classify pressure groups into which of the following categories?
o: State, market, civil society and electoral
accepted.x: Almond and Powell classify pressure groups as institutional, associational, non-associational and anomic.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact classification associated with the named scholars.
accepted.sec: Pressure groups - definition, types, most influential, techniques  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Spontaneous riots, demonstrations and agitations are examples of which type of pressure group activity?
accepted.x: Anomic pressure-group activity is characterised by spontaneous riots, demonstrations and agitations.
accepted.tq: Match the distinctive activity with the correct classification.
accepted.sec: Pressure groups - definition, types, most influential, techniques  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly matches a pressure-group technique with its meaning?
o: Propaganda — helping sympathetic candidates win elections
Electioneering — shaping public opinion through media and campaigns
Lobbying — dealing with legislators and officials regarding legislation and regulation
Propaganda — directly contesting elections to form the government
accepted.x: Lobbying means dealing with legislators and officials to promote or defeat legislation and regulation. Propaganda shapes public opinion, while electioneering assists sympathetic candidates.
accepted.tq: Separate the meanings of lobbying, propaganda and electioneering.
accepted.sec: Pressure groups - definition, types, most influential, techniques  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In the context of the APPSC classification of influential pressure groups, which organisation is identified as the most powerful pressure group?
accepted.x: The APPSC key identifies the All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC) as the most powerful pressure group.
accepted.tq: Recall the examination-specific identification of the influential group.
accepted.sec: Pressure groups - definition, types, most influential, techniques  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC), identified as India's oldest trade union in this context, was founded in:
accepted.x: AITUC was founded in 1920.
accepted.tq: Use the year-based numerical distinction among nearby historical dates.
accepted.sec: Pressure groups - definition, types, most influential, techniques  [APPSC]

accepted.s: N. M. Joshi is associated with AITUC as its:
accepted.x: N. M. Joshi was a co-founder of the All India Trade Union Congress.
accepted.tq: Match the personality with the specific organisational role.

accepted.s: A pressure group representing farmers or industrial workers primarily seeks to:
o: Replace the legislature through judicial orders
Conduct elections on behalf of the Election Commission
Exercise executive power over the concerned occupation
Press the government, legislators and bureaucracy for favourable laws and measures
accepted.x: Pressure groups represent sectional interests and press the government, legislators and bureaucracy for favourable laws and measures.
accepted.tq: Apply the definition of sectional representation to a governance situation.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following programmes and agencies in chronological order of their commencement:
A. DWCRA
B. SERP
C. Indira Kranthi Patham
D. MEPMA
accepted.x: DWCRA began in 1982-83, SERP and Velugu began in 2000, Indira Kranthi Patham began in 2004-05, and MEPMA began in 2007.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest programme first and then arrange the later milestones.
accepted.sec: SHG movement in AP - Velugu/IKP, SERP, MEPMA, DWCRA origins  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about DWCRA is correct?
o: It was a sub-scheme of IRDP for groups of rural women, initiated in 1982-83.
It was an urban poverty mission launched in 2007.
It was an interest subsidy programme introduced in 2004.
It was a World Bank-aided project implemented only in municipalities.
accepted.x: DWCRA was a sub-scheme of the Integrated Rural Development Programme for groups of rural women and began in 1982-83.
accepted.tq: Combine the programme's origin, target group and administrative relationship.
accepted.sec: SHG movement in AP - Velugu/IKP, SERP, MEPMA, DWCRA origins  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding SERP and Velugu:
1. SERP is a Society for Elimination of Rural Poverty established in 2000.
2. SERP implements rural SHG programmes in Andhra Pradesh.
3. Velugu was a World Bank-aided rural poverty project run by SERP.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. SERP was established in 2000, implements rural SHG programmes, and ran the World Bank-aided Velugu rural poverty project.
accepted.tq: Check whether the institutional identity, function and project relationship all align.
accepted.sec: SHG movement in AP - Velugu/IKP, SERP, MEPMA, DWCRA origins  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Indira Kranthi Patham was formed through the merger of:
accepted.x: Indira Kranthi Patham was formed in 2004-05 by merging Velugu and DWCRA and was implemented by SERP.
accepted.tq: Identify the merger partners rather than the implementing agency.
accepted.sec: SHG movement in AP - Velugu/IKP, SERP, MEPMA, DWCRA origins  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Pavala Vaddi, introduced in 2004, refers to:
o: A World Bank-aided rural poverty project
An interest subsidy for Self-Help Groups
A sub-scheme of IRDP for rural women
accepted.x: Pavala Vaddi was introduced in 2004 as an interest subsidy for Self-Help Groups.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the financial-support measure from the poverty programmes and agencies.
accepted.sec: SHG movement in AP - Velugu/IKP, SERP, MEPMA, DWCRA origins  [APPSC]

accepted.s: MEPMA is associated with which of the following?
o: Wholesale lending to NGOs for women borrowers
Rural poverty alleviation through a World Bank project
Urban Self-Help Groups and poverty reduction in municipal areas
accepted.x: MEPMA, or Mission for Elimination of Poverty in Municipal Areas, was established in 2007 for urban SHGs and poverty reduction.
accepted.tq: Use the rural-urban distinction to identify the correct mission.
accepted.sec: SHG movement in AP - Velugu/IKP, SERP, MEPMA, DWCRA origins  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Andhra Pradesh's Self-Help Group sector:
1. Andhra Pradesh ranks first in India in SHG-Bank Linkage.
2. Andhra Pradesh accounts for a 36% share at the national level.
3. The recovery rate is 99.66%.
4. The average disbursement is about ₹32,190 crore.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct: Andhra Pradesh ranks first, has a 36% national share, reports 99.66% recovery, and has an average disbursement of about ₹32,190 crore.
accepted.tq: Verify each numerical indicator independently before selecting the coded combination.

accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh SHGs use e-commerce platforms such as Amazon and Flipkart for selling their products.
accepted.tq: Distinguish commercial platforms from organisations and government agencies.

accepted.s: Rashtriya Mahila Kosh functions primarily through which lending model?
o: It lends to intermediary NGOs and microfinance bodies, which on-lend to poor women and SHGs.
It lends only to trade unions for industrial welfare.
It lends directly to every individual borrower without intermediaries.
It provides grants exclusively to municipal bodies for urban infrastructure.
accepted.x: Rashtriya Mahila Kosh follows a quasi-wholesale model: it lends to intermediary NGOs and microfinance bodies, which lend onward to poor women and SHGs.
accepted.tq: Identify the intermediary chain in the lending arrangement.
accepted.sec: Rashtriya Mahila Kosh - year, legal form, lending model  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Rashtriya Mahila Kosh is administered under which Union Ministry?
o: Ministry of Women and Child Development
Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
accepted.x: Rashtriya Mahila Kosh was set up under the Ministry of Women and Child Development.
accepted.tq: Apply the ministry-portfolio association without confusing it with the lending function.
accepted.sec: Rashtriya Mahila Kosh - year, legal form, lending model  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under which law was Rashtriya Mahila Kosh registered as a society?
o: Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969
accepted.x: Rashtriya Mahila Kosh is registered as a society under the Societies Registration Act, 1860.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the legal form and governing statute from company and cooperative legislation.
accepted.sec: Rashtriya Mahila Kosh - year, legal form, lending model  [APPSC]
